title: Plane hypersurface scheme, structural maps and structure-sheaf cohomology
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $d\in\mathbf N$, and let $F\in S=k[A,B,C]$ be homogeneous of degree $d$, with the total-degree grading [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}(S)=\mathbf P^2_k$ [def-pc-proj, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Define the ideal sheaf generated on $D_+(X_i)$ by $F/X_i^d$, without taking its radical. Its closed subscheme is $Z=\operatorname{Proj}(S/(F))$, with its specified closed immersion $\iota:Z\hookrightarrow P$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its structure morphism $\pi:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ induced by coefficients [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Define the scalar ring map $k\to\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ as pullback of constants by $\pi$. For $q\in\mathbf N$ define the $k$-module $H^q(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ by structure-sheaf module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], with scalars restricted along this scalar map. These constructions do not assume $F\ne0$, $d>0$, smoothness, reducedness, or irreducibility.
